transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess what made me come in is... well, after work or class, I’ll sit down with my laptop and I just end up eating a lot. Like, I'll eat a whole takeout meal, plus chips, sweets, and whatever other snacks I have stashed in my desk drawer. It's just way more than I ever planned to eat, and definitely more than I’d ever eat if I were around anyone else.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you've lost control over how much you're eating, or do you feel like you could stop if you really wanted to?

I definitely lose control. It's like... once I start, it feels like I’m just watching myself keep reaching for the next thing. Even while I’m doing it, I’m thinking to myself, Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish and you’re not even enjoying this anymore. But I just can't seem to stop once I'm in that mode.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to compensate or make up for what you ate, like exercising a lot, skipping meals, or anything else?

No, I don't really do anything like that. I mean, I don't throw up or take anything, and I definitely don't exercise a bunch to try and work it off. I usually just end up feeling really full and kind of miserable, and then I just try to get back to whatever I was doing, like my work or studying. But no, I don't do anything to make up for it.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, empty, or down most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely feel guilty and upset with myself right after I eat like that, but I don't feel sad or down most of the day. My mood is usually pretty normal, especially when I'm just going about my day at work or in class. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or anything.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F32.9 and F33.9 (Major Depressive Disorder) because patient denies persistent sadness/emptiness most of the day. F63.2 (Binge Eating Disorder) remains as the clear diagnosis: recurrent binge eating episodes with loss of control, no compensatory behaviors, and distress following episodes.
